t: This was the Public Record Office on Chancery Lane, in the City of London. From 1838 until 2003 it was the guardian of the United Kingdom's national archives, and it was under the control of the Master of the Rolls, a senior judge. In 2003 it merged with the Historical Manuscripts Commission to form The National Archives, which is based in Kew. The Public Record Office still exists as a legal entity. The building was designed by Sir James Pennethorne, an architect and planner particularly associated with buildings and parks in central London.
